title: 巨型向日葵与追太阳的秘密
pdf: https://michael-podcast-1513696684.cos.ap-chengdu.myqcloud.com/vol48/Vol48_晚读讲义_巨型向日葵与追太阳的秘密_v2.pdf

blocks.en: Hello, young explorers, and welcome back to Michael's Morning Listening! Today we step into a sunny garden. First, meet a little girl who grew a sunflower taller than a bus. Then, discover the secret: do sunflowers really follow the sun all day? Ready? Let's go!
blocks.title: 开场白
blocks.cn: 你好，小小探险家们，欢迎回到 Michael 的早听晚读！今天，我们走进一个洒满阳光的花园。首先，见见一位种出比巴士还高的向日葵的小姑娘。然后，揭开秘密：向日葵真的整天跟着太阳转吗？准备好了吗？出发！

blocks.en: In a small English town lives a five-year-old girl named Lucy. She joined a sunflower growing competition for children. She did not need anything expensive: just pots, compost and sunshine. Her approach was simple: she planted seeds in pots at the front of the house, where there was plenty of sunshine, and protected the shoots with old water bottles cut in half.
blocks.title: 巨型向日葵
blocks.cn: 在英国一个小镇上，住着一位五岁的小姑娘，名叫露西。她参加了一个小朋友种向日葵比赛。她不需要任何昂贵的东西：只要花盆、堆肥和阳光。她的方法很简单：把种子种在花盆里，放在屋前阳光充足的地方，再用剪开的旧水瓶保护幼苗。

blocks.en: It was not easy: she lost one plant, another fell over, and the wind blew the top off a third! But one plant kept growing and growing. Soon it was taller than her dad. At that altitude, Dad had to climb onto the car roof just to tie the plant to its canes! First one cane, then a longer one, then three canes tied together.
blocks.title: 巨型向日葵
blocks.cn: 这可不容易：她失去了一株，另一株倒了，还有一株的顶被风吹掉了！但有一株一直在长啊长。很快，它就比爸爸还高了。到了那个高度，爸爸不得不爬上车顶，才能把植株绑到竹竿上！先是一根竹竿，再是一根更长的，最后是三根绑在一起的竹竿。

blocks.en: Guess how tall it grew? 4.48 metres — taller than a double-decker bus! Lucy won the competition, and everyone celebrated her giant flower. And it did not cost much at all: just seeds, sunshine and patience. When the flower opened, sparrows came hoping for the precious seeds. Lucy showed us that even small hands can grow something huge.
blocks.title: 巨型向日葵
blocks.cn: 猜猜它长到了多高？4.48 米——比双层巴士还高！露西赢得了比赛，大家都为她的巨型向日葵庆祝。而且这花不了多少钱：只要种子、阳光和耐心。花儿开放的时候，麻雀们都飞来，希望吃到那些珍贵的种子。露西告诉我们，即使是小小的双手，也能种出巨大的东西。

blocks.en: Now: do sunflowers really follow the sun? The answer is yes — but only when they are young! A young sunflower turns its face from east in the morning to west in the evening, just as you turn your forehead toward the warm morning sun. At night, it quietly turns back to the east, ready for sunrise.
blocks.title: 追太阳的秘密
blocks.cn: 那么：向日葵真的会跟着太阳转吗？答案是肯定的——但只在它们还小的时候！一株年轻的向日葵，早上脸朝东，傍晚转到西，就像你把额头转向温暖的晨光一样。到了夜里，它又悄悄转回东方，准备迎接日出。

blocks.en: How does it move? It does not spin like a machine. The secret is in the stem: water and liquid food travel up inside the stem, and the tissue on the shaded side grows faster, so the stem bends slowly toward the light. Scientists call this daily dance heliotropism: a slow, steady pulse, like the plant's own inner clock.
blocks.title: 追太阳的秘密
blocks.cn: 它是怎么动的呢？它可不是像机器那样旋转。秘密藏在茎里：水和液体养分在茎里往上走，背阴一侧的组织长得更快，于是茎就慢慢弯向阳光。科学家把这种每天的舞蹈叫做 heliotropism（向日性）：就像植物自己身体里的时钟，缓慢而稳定地跳动。

blocks.en: But the most surprising aspect: when the flower grows up, it stops dancing! A mature sunflower stays facing east all day. Why? An east-facing flower warms up fast in the morning, and warm flowers attract more bees. Scientists conducted an experiment: they turned some flowers to face west, and the east-facing flowers attracted five times as many pollinators! So the sunflower's trick is not just following the sun — it is knowing when to stop.
blocks.title: 追太阳的秘密
blocks.cn: 但最令人惊讶的一面是：花儿长大后，它就不跳舞了！一株成熟的向日葵整天都脸朝东。为什么呢？朝东的花儿早上暖和得快，而温暖的花儿能吸引更多的蜜蜂。科学家做过一个实验：他们把一些花儿转朝西，结果朝东的花儿吸引的授粉昆虫是朝西的五倍！所以，向日葵的本事不只是跟着太阳转——而是知道什么时候该停下来。

blocks.en: Today's idiom is "a wild goose chase." It means a search for something you will probably never find. For example: looking for one tiny seed in a huge field is a wild goose chase! And hunting for Lucy's lost water bottle all over the garden? That would be a wild goose chase too! But growing a sunflower is not a wild goose chase: with sunshine, water and patience, you will really see it grow. Try it this week: tell your family about a wild goose chase you once had!
blocks.title: 今日俚语
blocks.cn: 今天的俚语是“a wild goose chase”（追野鹅）。它的意思是寻找一件你可能永远找不到的东西。举个例子：在一片大田里找一颗小小的种子，就是 a wild goose chase！在整个花园里找一个丢了的水瓶，也是 a wild goose chase！但种向日葵可不是 a wild goose chase：有了阳光、水和耐心，你真的能看到它长大。这周试试用它：跟家人说说你经历过的一次 a wild goose chase！

blocks.en: Now it is your turn! Two questions for you. One: Lucy's sunflower grew 4.48 metres tall. Can you find something near your home about that tall? Two: a young sunflower follows the sun, but a grown-up one faces east. Why do you think facing east helps the flower? Talk about it with your family!
blocks.title: 结束语与互动问题
blocks.cn: 现在轮到你们啦！两个问题考考你。第一：露西的向日葵长到了 4.48 米高。你能在家附近找到差不多这么高的东西吗？第二：一株年轻的向日葵跟着太阳转，但长大了的向日葵脸朝东。你觉得为什么脸朝东对花儿有帮助？和家人聊聊吧！

blocks.en: That is all for today, young explorers. We appreciate you listening and learning with us. Keep your eyes open, keep asking questions, and we will meet tomorrow morning. Goodbye, and have a wonderful day!
blocks.title: 告别
blocks.cn: 今天的节目就到这里啦，小小探险家们。感谢你们和我们一起听、一起学。保持好奇，继续提问，我们明天早上再见。再见，祝你度过美好的一天！

quiz.title: B. 单项选择（Single Choice）
questions:
How tall did Lucy's sunflower grow?
A. 2.04 metres
B. 3.02 metres
C. 4.48 metres
D. 9.17 metres

What did Lucy use to protect the young shoots?
A. Old water bottles
B. Plastic bags
C. Glass jars
D. Paper boxes

What does a young sunflower do during the day?
A. It stays facing east
B. It turns from east to west
C. It turns from west to east
D. It does not move at all

What does "a wild goose chase" mean?
A. A race with geese
B. A search you will probably never finish
C. A trip to a farm
D. A dance in the garden

children.text: Scientists conducted an experiment: they turned some flowers to face west, and the east-facing flowers attracted five times as many pollinators!
：conduct（进行）+ an experiment（一个实验），意思是“做了一个实验”。conduct 后面常常跟 experiment、research（研究）、survey（调查）这类词。
turned some flowers to face west
：turn（转动、转朝）+ some flowers（一些花儿）+ to face west（朝向西边），意思是“把一些花儿转得朝向西边”。to face 在这里表示转动后的方向。
：five times（五倍）+ as many（和……一样多）+ pollinators（授粉昆虫，可数名词复数），意思是“五倍数量的授粉昆虫”。说“是另一方的五倍”时，英语就用“数字 + times as many + 复数名词”。
做实验（conducted an experiment）→ 转花朝西（turned some flowers to face west）→ 数结果（five times as many pollinators）
。一句话里藏着固定搭配、方向结构和倍数表达三个机关。
"protected the shoots with old water bottles cut in half."
"A young sunflower turns its face from east in the morning to west in the evening."
"It means a search for something you will probably never find."
D. Your own translations — there is no key for this part. Read your Chinese aloud and check that it sounds natural.

words.clue: A large wild bird with a long neck, the bird in a saying about a search that finds nothing. Example: a wild ___ chase.
A tall garden plant with a big yellow head that turns to follow bright light. Example: a little girl who grew a ___ taller than a bus.
A slow steady beat, like a living thing's own inner rhythm. Example: a slow, steady ___, like the plant's own inner clock.
Small brown garden birds that love to eat tiny seeds. Example: ___s came hoping for the precious seeds.
A long thin stick used to hold up a tall plant. Example: then three ___s tied together.
A long search for something hard to find, often a waste of effort. Example: a wild goose ___.
The soft living material inside a stem that grows on one side. Example: the ___ on the shaded side grows faster.
An insect, like a bee, that carries dust from one bloom to another so seeds can form. Example: attracted five times as many ___s!
A tiny hard grain that a plant grows from. Example: looking for one tiny ___ in a huge field.
One surprising side of a thing. Example: the most surprising ___: when the flower grows up, it stops dancing!
